I'm probably just biased against pikes from the last time I kept one. I was 14 years old and I hooked one that was almost 6 feet long. I fought quite a while to bring it in the boat. That bugger took up a lot of space. We got back to our cabin (thankfully we were leaving on this day) and my dad didn't want to bring it back to the city, but I convinced him we should because if we have it to the neighbors, they would cook it and share with us. So I used 2 garbage bags that didn't cover the whole fish (middle was exposed) and stuffed him head first into the biggest cooler we had with ice, and most of his body was out. Driving home for hours he was flapping around occasionally and we delivered a live fish. They cooked it up in a few ways: a soup, some steaks and some tacos. All 3 ways had bones. It could just be their prepping skill, but just comparing it to the pickerels we gave them in the past, never an issue.

Finding bones when there shouldn't be any can ruin a meal for sure, I mean I have no problem eating cooked whole fish with the bones in. I usually don't fillet perch and I never fillet trout, but I expect there to be bones and I cook them to be easy to eat around the bones, finding bones in filleted and prepared meals sucks though and ruins it for sure..
